Subject: Re: SOW draft for capacity bump — initial comments

Vanessa, thank you — Marta from EdgeHealth. We reviewed the SOW draft and have a handful of high-level asks before legal will route internally:

- We need a concise definition of the new SKU (GPU-hour vs. concurrent sessions). The procurement team prefers a SKU tied to committed throughput not raw GPU hours.
- Price floor: can you confirm if the uplift price is a one-time add or amortized monthly?
- Implementation milestones: our PM wants clearer handoffs and an acceptance sign-off checklist (3 steps).

Attaching our internal checklist and a small markup of the SOW. Can we lock in a single point of contact for legal redlines? Contracts@edgehealth will collate, but they'll escalate technical scope questions to Marta.

Best,
Marta
Head of Platform Partnerships
EdgeHealth

Marta — thanks for the quick read and the checklist, very helpful. Looping in Karthik (sales) for commercial points and Laura (legal) for contract language.

Quick answers up front:
- SKU model: Redwood prefers committed throughput (concurrent inference units) for predictability. We'll propose an exhibit that maps committed RU to an equivalent GPU-hour baseline for reporting transparency.
- Pricing treatment: the uplift is typically amortized over the current term unless the customer asks for a one-time invoice. We can present both options.
- Acceptance: agree — we'll add a tight 3-step acceptance checklist with sign-off fields.

Laura / Karthik — attached is the EdgeHealth markup. Can you propose consolidated redline language and confirm whether we can map to a new Exhibit (Exhibit G) that contains SKU mappings + acceptance criteria?

Thanks
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Team — I reviewed Marta's notes. Commercially I prefer the committed-concurrency SKU (simpler for monthly billing). Two asks from my side:

1) Can we offer an amortized uplift by default and call out a one-time invoice as an opt-in? That keeps renewal math clean.
2) For the Exhibit, include an example conversion table (Committed RU -> estimated GPU-hour/month) and a note: "Conversion is for billing transparency and not a hard cap on burst usage."

Markus: can you confirm operational feasibility for the acceptance checklist milestones (we'll need infra involvement for step 2 — production cutover smoke tests).

Karthik
Director, Sales

On boarding cadence: propose internal review cycle: legal redline draft by EOD Mon, consolidated reply to EdgeHealth Tue, target signature by end of month if no major policy blockers.

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com

Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 14:18:00 -0700

Vanessa / Karthik — draft redlines attached. Key legal notes:

- I created a new Exhibit G (SKU Mapping & Acceptance). It contains: SKU definitions, billing mapping table, and a 3-step acceptance checklist (Dev handoff, Smoke Test, Production Acceptance Sign-off).
- Pricing clause: added an amortization default clause and an explicit opt-in checkbox for one-time invoicing.
- Liability/ SLA: clarified that the committed-concurrency SKU carries the standard SLA; any burst beyond committed levels is subject to a best-effort priority and billed per the overage rates in Exhibit B.
- Termination/rollback: added a 30-day notice for capacity downscales to make sure we can reallocate pools.

I kept the redlines minimal and flagged two non-negotiables the legal team will not accept without exec approval: (1) removal of the termination notice when it impacts reserved capacity; (2) shifting data residency language out of the DPA.

Next steps: Vanessa, please obtain confirmation from EdgeHealth that Exhibit G is acceptable in principle. If they push back on the termination notice, we need to escalate to Ops and GTM for a mitigation note.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
